Critter Potato Gun

Critters are raiding your potato pile. Defend it with a potato gun — every shot costs a potato.

How to Play

✋

Left hand loads — pinch to load a potato

👉

Right hand shoots — pinch to fire

💪

Left hand pinch again loads a HEAVY — pinch twice to stack two potatoes, one big shot

Hands only. Play seated.

Two Ways to Play

🌙

The Night — Survive the night — round by round, as long as the pile lasts

♾️

Endless Night — No rounds — survive as long as you can

Hands-only WebXR · Opens in your Quest Browser

For the full real-wall experience, scan your room first: Settings → Environment setup → Space settings

Built for Meta VR Glasses · Playable on Quest 3

Downloads — grab the build

The orange button builds critter-potato-gun-usb-test-v10.21.37.zip in your browser at click time — it fetches this page's own current HTML as the game's index.html, adds the launcher script and a server.js on port 8901, so the ZIP always contains the newest build, never a stale copy. Extract all three files into the Game folder (overwriting), then run the launcher as usual. (These are the launcher panel's own buttons. Since v10.21.3 this panel is the very first block on the page, with Enter AR and the diagnostics panel directly beneath it — always on top, never buried.)

A hand entering tracking already pinched, or jittering across a single threshold, can no longer fire, load or stack; every edge the guard turns away is counted here by cause. Since v10.15.5 the browser's own 'select' events pass through the SAME gate (new cause: select-gate) — the v10.15.3 exemption is closed. Since v10.21.5 the guard also carries a DELIBERATE-PINCH RESCUE: a close the guard suppressed (no-open / reacquire / select-gate) whose hand stays cleanly pinched for ~140 ms past its window is treated as ONE deliberate pinch and counted on this line as a rescue — every gate is unchanged, and jitter or an entry phantom can never hold a clean close that long. Since v10.21.7 the reacquire window is DEBOUNCED (the audit confirmed it restarted on flicker): joint dropouts and input-source absences shorter than ~120 ms are bridged — the window is measured from the last stable tracked moment and the channel state (seen-open, rescue dwell) survives the dropout — while a lapse of ≥120 ms lapses exactly as before, so a hand entering tracking already pinched still cannot act. Since v10.21.10 the rescue demands a CORROBORATED clean close — the fingertip must hold within 3.5 cm of its dwell anchor and collapsed-point joint estimates (thumb and finger read as the same point) never count — so frustum-edge noise trains and debounce-stitched flicker cannot rescue into phantom loads/fires; the select rescue likewise restarts if the wrist moves >6 cm and is cancelled when fresh joints show the hand clearly open. SELECT-CHANNEL ARBITRATION (v10.21.10): a select the gate suppresses still acts IMMEDIATELY when its hand has been continuously tracked for ≥0.6 s — at steep down-angles the joint channel degrades first and the OS recogniser is the surviving witness — while a hand that appears already pinched has no such tenure and stays gated; arbitrated actions count on this line. PILE-DEFENCE CONTEXT (v10.21.10): with the gaze on the pile footprint or on a beetle within ~1.15 m of the pile, the evidence bar is the rescue's bar (a corroborated ~140 ms held close acts, reacquire window waived, dwell bridges dropouts) — a named, bounded, counted rule; everywhere else the full hysteresis bar stands. v10.21.30: on the COMBAT path that bar is retired — Meta's own 'select' (pinch) and 'squeeze' (grab) events act ungated as the primary trigger (see the diag-236 line); the hysteresis machinery now gates panel picks and the deduped joint-backup channel only.
  • Auto-pause (v10.15.5): no auto-pause yet this page session — if both hands leave tracking for >3 s mid-run, the game pauses itself and now SAYS so in-headset (“⏸ PAUSED — HANDS LOST”, big banner) instead of stopping silently like a freeze. This line counts those pauses for the whole page session and names the round / wave / pile of the last one, so a mid-run “freeze” can be convicted as the auto-pause — or cleared of it — from the paste alone. Resume is unchanged: raise both hands into view. Since v10.21.1 this line also counts tracking-loss events and how each pause recovered (hands / select): posed-but-joint-dead tracking (hands visible to the pose chain, joints dead — Robert's recording freeze) now engages the same visible pause, a controller trigger resumes it and the controller is adopted cleanly, and no state leaves input dead while the session lives. Since v10.21.6 this line also carries “session focus lost ×N · recovered ×N”: a focus loss is the XR session's visibility leaving focused-visible mid-run (the Quest universal menu opening over the game — the OS palm-pinch gesture, which no game can open or block); at the transition ALL stale pinch/select/gesture state is cleared and the hands-lost clock restarts at refocus, so closing the menu hands back a live game — the hands-lost pause (if it engaged) resumes by raising hands or a select, exactly as designed, and “recovered” counts when play actually resumes afterwards.
  • Content Pass II (v10.15.5 — fix pass on the v10.15.4 frame-lifetime repair): — — Golden Rush (once per run, Round 2+, guaranteed by Round 4, 20 s window, +2 🥔 per Golden killed inside it) · Difficulty (start-panel selector, snapshotted at run start — a live run never changes; the tutorial is always Standard) · Tuber moth (Round 3+, ~1 in 12, max 2 alive, counts toward the beetle cap). · Queen drama (v10.21): a suffix on this line counts arrivals staged / death spectacles / breach pops (Module J, QDR21).

Each guarantee fires at most once and only if the run reaches that point; each reads armed / spent / not reached here. Later runs in the same page session use the normal rarity curves, untouched.
  • Orbs (v10.16): — — the three orb kinds that always existed (Frost / Frenzy / Splash — drop rules and effects unchanged) now each look like their effect (ice crystal with icicle spikes / golden fry burst / orange sweet potato), carry a floating name tag, earn a one-line Keeper explanation on their first drop of a page session, and stage their effect visibly on collection (frost creep + an in-world power chip counting down). This line records which kinds have dropped and what is active.
  • Fallback damage (v10.16): — — in fallback mode only (no room scan), crack decals now visibly spread from each breach across the ring as rounds progress, a growing breach gets an extra plaster burst + dust puff, and a patch leaves a matte wall-toned seam (scars list, cap 26 — re-toned matte in v10.21.1, both modes). Real-plane mode is unchanged and this line says so.
  • Real-plane model (v10.21.6 — DROP DESCENT + BREACH-HOST DISTANCE CAP; ring travel restored in v10.20.2, the emergency lever): scanned rooms keep real-plane BREACHES, scars and crack damage on the real walls (front-180° bearing rule unchanged — a wall behind you is scenery only) and the latched scanned floor height (FLOOR_EFF, ≤6 cm refinements) — but beetle TRAVEL is the fallback floor-ring model, NOT room conformance: emerge UPRIGHT at the breach mouth (eyes telegraph as always) → a straight world-space DROP down the breach's own vertical line to the latched floor (~0.35–0.5 s, dust puff + small bounce on landing) → floor lanes to the pile. There is NO wall crawl and NO crawl orientation in scanned rooms any more — the v10.20.2 scurry is deleted (it floated off the wall face and could run upside-down). Carriers return along the floor to below their breach, then climb the same vertical line into the mouth. NEW breaches host only on true walls — large vertical planes whose polygon reaches within ~0.35 m of the floor (mirrors, picture frames and furniture sides are excluded when a real wall exists) — and, since v10.21.2, only within HOST RANGE: the breach anchor must sit within 8.0 m (~26 ft) of the session origin (BREACH_HOST_RANGE212, defined once in breachSites). Out-of-range walls never host; if no qualifying wall is in range, the fallback ring hosts the room instead, and the Room line above reports which state the current room is in. There is NO in-plane crawl routing, NO host-surface assignment and NO furniture steering in scanned rooms. Shot resolution in scanned rooms: beetles first (body tolerance as before) → WALL planes (splats on walls/breaches as before) → the floor at the latched height. FURNITURE PLANES NEVER BLOCK SHOTS. Retired after headset failures in this room: surface-conforming travel (v10.16.2), deterministic routes (v10.20.1), furniture steer-around (v10.20.1) and the wall scurry (v10.21.1). Since v10.21.5 the host rule is ABSOLUTE (Robert's v10.21.4 session had breach holes in the ceiling ~2 ft in front of him, over the pile, with carriers climbing a bare line back up into them): the breach anchor must sit 1.2–8.0 m out — never practically over the pile — the top-up from lesser planes (mirror, painting, furniture side) is deleted, so a scanned room with too few true walls is RING-hosted for its remaining sites; emergence portals in scanned rooms come only through walls or the floor (the ceiling roll is deleted); and scars may attach only to the same true-wall set, projected FLUSH onto the host plane. Fallback-ring mode (no scan) is byte-unchanged. Since v10.21.6 the AIRBORNE PATH is audited end-to-end (mouth → emergence → drop → first floor-lane step, plus the carrier climb): the v10.21.1 sim had measured only the drop segment, which was honest — the forward drift Robert reported lived in the EMERGENCE segment: pickSpawn lerps a scanned wall spawn 5% toward the pile (up to ~0.26 m off the wall face at the 5.2 m candidate limit, and clampToPlaneRect preserves that off-plane offset) and doSpawn pushes the body a further r×0.85 proud of the surface, and drop211Arm adopted that pushed position as the drop line — so the beetle emerged floating off the wall face and dropped there, visibly in front of the wall. FIX: when a drop arms on a beetle with a host plane, the drop line (and the body) is re-seated IN the mouth plane — plane-local normal offset zeroed — so the whole airborne phase stays on the breach's own vertical line, deviation 0 by construction (the requirement was ≤ body radius); beetles without a host snap (ring-hosted breaches) keep their spawn line, whose only offset was the proud push (r×0.85 < r). The carrier climb already rides dropX/dropZ, so the return trip inherits the corrected line. The drop model itself (timing, ease, bounce, dust) is unchanged.
  • Wave guard (v10.16.1 · route re-plans v10.20.1): no recalls or re-plans yet — if a live wave makes no progress (no kill, steal, spawn or resolution) for ~45 s while beetles remain alive, the stalest beetle is recalled — it burrows out where it stands, counts as resolved, and the wave moves on. The Queen is exempt. One beetle can never soft-lock a run again. Since v10.20.1 (model per v10.20.2) a beetle that makes no progress for ~5 s re-plans on its own — under the ring model that is just a fresh lane: a wall beetle drops to the floor, a floor beetle hops sideways — and every re-plan is counted on this line, so a freeze names itself here long before the 45 s recall.
  • Augments (v10.18): no augment cards offered yet this page session — two temporary gun add-ons join the Harvest Choice draw from the choice that opens Round 2 onward (never during the tutorial, never the one already live): ⚡ Chain Spud (20 s — every hit arcs lightning to the nearest beetle within ~1.2 m, 1 damage) and ➶ Piercing Rounds (20 s — a shot punches through the first beetle and can bite one more behind it, same potato). One at a time; the gun wears the mod (copper coils / brass lance) with a countdown chip over the pile; counters here are page-session totals.
  • Frenzy (v10.20): no charges yet this page session — kills charge the SPUD FRENZY meter (standard +1 · Golden +2 · HEAVY +2 · full at 12 · no charge in the tutorial · no recharge inside the window); at full charge the Keeper's crate of rejects pays for 10 s of loads and shots — same pinch and HEAVY rules, the pile simply is not decremented — while the crate beside the pile visibly depletes and the gun glows gold. The window's clock runs in the playing phase only: it survives a round transition with time remaining and ends at run start / game over. Counters here are page-session totals.
  • Shot endings (v10.21.14): no shots counted yet this page session — every shot that dies is tallied by what ended it, in the loop's resolution order (orbs → eggs → spit blobs → beetles, each on the swept segment with the beetle body-tolerance allowance → wall planes → the latched floor → life expiry / below-floor cull). “Wall plane” endings land on the detected vertical planes' collision rectangles — since v10.21.14 centred on each polygon's REAL centre, not its plane origin (an off-centre polygon used to grow an invisible wall past the real wall's edge: shots stopping mid-air). If a future session still shows shots dying short, this line says on what.

  • Watchdog (v10.10): no frame errors caught — the frame loop catches its own exceptions and logs them here. The same error 3× disables the implicated system for the session, named here. Last session diagnostics

Saved automatically while you play (build + time stamped). If this page reloads after a session — the Quest Browser can discard the tab while you upload video — the played session's counters survive here instead of resetting to zero.

No saved session yet — play a session and this fills in.
1 · Aim — Head by default (v10.3)

Aim: Head is the default: the gun rides low in your view and points exactly where you look — the mode that proved far easier seated, especially for floor targets (arm aiming puts your hand where your knees are). Aim: Hand (shoulder-line) is still available: the gun sits in your hand and the barrel follows the line from your shoulder to your hand. Switch any time in the pause menu or with the 🎯 button below; the diagnostics Aim line shows the mode. Note: menu and Harvest Choice picks always use gaze + pinch, whichever Aim mode is on.

2 · Reload — Manual by default (v10.5)

Manual: the hands are split — your LEFT hand loads, your RIGHT hand only fires. Gun empty? Pinch with your left hand (thumb to index finger), anywhere, looking anywhere — no gaze at the pile needed: a potato arcs from the pile into the hopper and the pile pays. One pinch = one load, guaranteed: nothing loads on its own, and the right hand can never load. Heavy shot: left hand again — pinch with your left hand again while one potato is chambered — the second pinch stacks a second potato on top: that is the one and only HEAVY gesture, and it seats the HEAVY round (deep clunk + HEAVY LOADED callout) for one huge Tank-killing splat. Auto: flip the 🥔 Reload toggle (below or in the pause menu) and the gun loads the next standard round itself after each shot.

3 · Fire — pinch the trigger

Pinch with the gun hand; the shot leaves the muzzle along the barrel. Watch for power-up orbs from Golden/Carrier kills — there are three kinds, and since v10.16 each one looks like what it does and wears a floating name tag: ❄ Frost (a saturated ice-blue crystal with icicle spikes — shoot it and your shots freeze beetles for 12 s, each frozen beetle encased in a jagged blue crystal shell), 🍟 Frenzy (a golden fry burst — 8 s of rapid fire, no reload, every shot dragging a golden sparkle trail), 🍠 Splash (an orange sweet potato — your next 5 shots burst, each burst drawing its orange radius ring). Shoot one to activate it; the effect is staged where you can see it, with a chip over the pile counting it down.

In the flat 3D preview the same rules apply with a mouse, so you can learn the scene anywhere: drag to look around the front field, click anywhere to load (double-click loads a HEAVY double shot), click a beetle to fire at it. The preview is a rehearsal — judge distance, speed and pinch feel only in the headset. Pausing: in AR, pinch with your LEFT hand and HOLD for 1 second — the only in-AR opener since v10.7, the floating MENU button is deleted — to freeze the game and open the in-world menu, then LOOK at a menu button (the orange gaze dot is the only cursor; the gun holsters while a menu is open) and pinch to choose it; in the preview, use the ⏸ Pause / Menu button. Wristband radar: glance at your LEFT wrist during AR play — blips show beetles relative to where you face. In the preview it docks at the lower-left of the view.

Meta VR Start Developer Competition 2026

They're after your potatoes. Your ammo is your potatoes.

Potato beetles burst out of your walls, ceiling and furniture in mixed reality — and you defend the pile with a two-hand potato gun, firing the very potatoes they're stealing. Grab a potato from the pile, drop it in the gun, pinch to fire. Seated, front 180° only. No controllers, no buttons, hands only.

Pop detonations throw a ring of pulp stars; the Husk's shell-break throws two flying shell halves; the moth's corkscrew was already Module D3's and is untouched. ④ COLONY PERSONALITY — the breach taunt ladder gains five cockier rungs for late rounds, a nervous set replaces the chalk once a Queen has fallen that sitting, and the Queen now warns you from inside the wall — a rumble, eyes in the main breach, and a line — a few seconds BEFORE her Round 3 entrance. ⑤ THREE NEW COMIC GAGS through the existing tone() engine and the SAME shared ~4 s gag limiter (so they can never stack with the trombone or the whistle): a spring boing for Pop bursts and Husk breaks, a tiny kazoo fanfare for a Golden Rush that actually pays out, and a deflating whistle when a run ends at grade D. ⑥ HIT JUICE — golden kills burst coin-sparkles; Out of your real walls — over your real desk, aimed your way

Power-up orbs · v10.16 — every orb looks like its effect

Power-up orbs — what they look like, what they do

Orbs drop where certain beetles die (Golden and Carrier kills, clean one-shot kills, and Tank weak-point kills). Shoot an orb to activate it — the activation shot is free: your loaded potato stays loaded. The orb fades after ~10 seconds, so decide fast. There are exactly three kinds:

  • ❄ Frost orb — a saturated ice-blue crystal with icicle spikes (v10.16.2: deep azure, white only as glints — never a white blob). Shoot it and you get Frost Potatoes for 12 seconds: every hit freezes that beetle solid for 2 seconds (a frozen beetle cannot move, flee or steal for its full 2 seconds). On collection, frost visibly creeps over every living beetle — a jagged blue crystal shell with icicle spikes and fracture lines, not a milky bubble — and a chip over the pile counts the 12 seconds down.
  • 🍟 Frenzy orb — a deep-gold ball with french-fry sticks bursting out of the top. Shoot it and you get French Fry Frenzy for 8 seconds (longer with the Harvest card): no reloading at all — just keep pinching; each shot pulls 1 potato straight from the pile. While it runs, every shot in flight drags a golden sparkle trail — the frenzy is visible, not just counted.
  • 🍠 Splash orb — a deep-orange sweet potato with a green sprout. Shoot it and your next 5 shots burst on impact, damaging every beetle in a small radius around the hit — and each burst now draws its orange radius ring at the impact, so you can see exactly what the splash covered. The answer to Brood families and Pop chains.

Each orb carries a floating name tag while it drifts (“❄ FROST — shoot it!”), the first time a kind drops in a session the Keeper explains it in one line, and collecting one always stages the effect where you can see it — a named popup, a burst at the pile, and the countdown chip. No invisible effects, and no two kinds can be confused at a glance.

🔧 Gun augments (v10.18) — power-ups that bolt onto the gun itself. Two new Harvest Choice cards join the pick-1-of-3 from the choice that opens Round 2 onward (never during the tutorial, and never the augment you already have live): ⚡ Chain Spud — for 20 s, every shot that bites arcs lightning to the nearest other beetle within ~1.2 m for 1 damage, while copper coils crackle around the barrel; ➶ Piercing Rounds — for 20 s, a shot punches through the first beetle and can bite one more directly behind it on the same potato, wearing an elongated brass lance with a glowing ring. One augment at a time (picking the other replaces it and restarts the 20 s), it runs alongside the orbs and your ammo choice, HEAVY shots benefit too, a chip over the pile counts it down, expiry fizzles on the gun — and it never makes a shot free: the potato economy is untouched.

🥔 Spud Frenzy (v10.20) — the build-up meter. Kills charge a 12-segment ring beside the pile chips (a tick and a pop per segment): a standard kill +1, a Golden or HEAVY kill +2. When it fills, the Keeper rolls out a crate of rejects — “misfits, too ugly to defend, perfect to shoot” — and for 10 seconds the crate pays for every load and shot instead of the pile. Loading works exactly as always (same pinches, same HEAVY stacks, same load authority); only the bill changes, and the crate beside the pile visibly empties as you draw from it. The gun glows warm gold, a countdown chip joins the pile chips, the meter does not recharge during its own window, and gun augments and orbs overlap it freely.

New in v10.21.12 — the two approved scoring adds (Module K, staging only, stacked on v10.21.10; peel-back is v10.21.10). ① 🌙 Night Falls: ▶ PLAY (and only ▶ PLAY — ONE MORE NIGHT and Restart stay instant) now opens with a ~3.5 s staged sting: the music ducks, a low swell rises, the colony’s eyes blink open across the breaches left to right, one Keeper line lands (“Night falls. The colony is awake — and it is hungry.” — it replaces the stock run-start line, never stacks on it), the pile trembles once with a soft thump, and only then does Wave 1 spawn. No spawns, timers or scoring run during the sting; look around freely; any pinch skips it to the identical end state. On a first-ever browser the sting plays first, then the tutorial begins exactly as stock. Stings staged / skipped are counted on the diagnostics Front door line. ② 🏁 The final score card: the results panel’s top is now a designed moment — the grade letter LARGE beside the final score, a headline row of three Ledger stats (best combo · clutch saves · potatoes kept), and the Keeper’s grade verdict, scaling in over ~1 s with a small sting when the panel opens. Any pinch lands the beat instantly and the buttons work on that same pinch — ONE MORE NIGHT is never blocked. The orange OPENED-VIA pill is demoted to small plain text under the title, the duplicated score/clutch lines leave the header (the card carries them once), the button stack drops one even slot and the Ledger hangs below it with the same clear gaps — the full Ledger below is byte-for-byte the v10.21.10 readable layout. ③ Menu polish audit: every panel and chip was re-checked against the text-containment rule — findings and fixes are listed in the audit notes for this build (headline: a Harvest card’s third sub-line could touch its quip; it now draws tighter with a clear gap). Module K is one strippable module behind one flag (STAGE11.enabled): flag off, the game is exactly v10.21.10. No mechanics, balance, spawn, economy, input or travel code changed.

New in v10.21.5 — the repair pass from your v10.21.4 session footage (stacked on v10.21.4; protected systems untouched except at the named seams). Eight fixes: the Queen's arrival is unmissable now — banner at the gate, a breach that shakes and swells for the full build, bigger cracks that persist, and a staging counter that increments on every real spawn. The breach void stays dark — the glow is a rim ring, never a filled cream disc. Breaches and scars host only on true walls — the ceiling roll is deleted, the top-up from paintings and furniture sides is gone, anchors sit 1.2–8 m out, and scars are flat crack seams flush on the wall. The Husk wears its cracked tan shell again. Narration lines take turns — one at a time, no more glyph collisions. Recenter is arm-and-lock — the button moved under the panel header; pinch it, look where you want the panel, and it locks in ~2 s. The Keeper's Ledger reads bigger — larger type, taller panel, flavour sheds before stats shrink. And deliberate pinches are rescued — if the guard eats a pinch but your hand holds it closed, it acts once, and the Input guard line counts the rescues. Underneath, the v10.21.4 build added the one-click Copy diagnostics button, and the v10.21.3 build was the flat-page layout reorder (this page opens with the downloads panel at the very top, Enter AR + diagnostics directly beneath it), and the v10.21.2 build brought the freeze-eve repair + the breach-host distance cap (stacked on v10.21; every protected system untouched). From your v10.21 session: the wall-scurry descent is deleted — beetles now emerge upright and drop straight down from the breach to the floor (no more floating off the wall, nothing upside-down, nothing descending mid-room), and new breaches only open on true walls, never on mirrors, frames or the tower. The breach void is dark again (amber ring, bright eyes) and the pale hexagon family — scars and rim plaster — is matte and wall-toned. The tracking freeze is hardened: hands that pose with dead joints now trigger the visible HANDS LOST pause, and a controller trigger both resumes and works. No narration renders across an open panel any more, and panel backdrops now contain every row of their content, quips included. Augments were traced, not touched: the eligibility gate is provably open — three misses is ~16% luck. And two panel fixes from the same session: the corrective re-place is now thresholded and eased (no more latch glitch when you turn your head as a panel opens), and the pause + start panels carry a 🧭 Recenter panel button that re-anchors every panel to the way you are facing now. And the distance cap you settled: new breaches now host only within 8 m (~26 ft) of where you sit — a 20+ ft living room keeps its far wall in play from the couch, and only hall-sized spaces fall back to the ring. No balance changes ride along: distance buys shooting time but costs aim, and there are no leaderboards. Use the v10.21.5 ZIP from the download buttons at the very top of this page.

New in v10.21 — Boss & Big Moments (staging only, stacked on v10.20.2; travel, spawns, balance, economy, controls and every protected system untouched).

The Queen’s entrance is now a boss arrival: for ~3.4 seconds her breach shakes harder and harder while dust and debris patter down the wall, cracks erupt outward in three bursts (and stay as damage), the music ducks under a low rising sting, and the eyes in the dark flare — then she tears through in a plaster explosion with a 120 ms dramatic beat, and a low pulsing boss layer plays under the music for as long as she lives. Her death is staged too: bigger burst, a colony wail, a shorter dramatic beat. Even an ordinary new breach now pops open with a small shake, crack burst and sting. None of it blocks play, and it all quiets down behind an open panel instead of freezing. The Content Pass II diagnostics line now ends with the Queen drama counts, so a paste proves it fired. Use the v10.21 ZIP from the download buttons at the top of this section.

New in v10.20.2 — the ring-travel restoration (the emergency lever; scanned-room travel + shot resolution only, everything else untouched). Three successive real-plane travel layers have now failed in your room three different ways, so the conformance model is retired, not patched. Your v10.20.1 evidence named the last mechanism: beetles bunched in front of the inversion table and sat (stall → re-plan → stall), and shots splatted above them — the scanned furniture plane is a filled rectangle in code, a phantom solid that deadlocked floor steering on the approach lane and ate shots fired down at beetles beside it. Zero kills also fully explains the Frenzy ×0 — no kills, no charges; Frenzy itself was never broken. Scanned rooms now travel exactly like the fallback ring that ran cleanly for days: emerge from the real wall breach, one straight scurry down the wall face to the floor at the breach's base, then floor lanes to the pile at the latched scanned floor height; Carriers haul home along the floor, then climb. Furniture is out of travel and out of shot resolution entirely — shots resolve beetles → walls → floor, so a splat can never again land on an invisible surface above a beetle. Kept from the real-plane stack, all verified by you: breaches, scars and crack theatre on your real walls, the floor-height latch, the wave guard. The Real-plane diagnostics line now states this model plainly, so your next paste proves the lever build is live. Use the v10.20.2 ZIP from the download buttons at the top of this section.

New in v10.20.1 — the deterministic-route repair (repair only, stacked on v10.20; no art, mechanics, balance or content changes). Your v10.20 session in the scanned room showed the travel layer failing on real geometry: beetles froze, dropped straight down out of breaches, floated up a foot or two mid-walk, hovered at couch height, and overlapped each other. The causes were all in surface assignment being re-derived per tick — worst of them, the furniture-climb memory re-rolled its coin every frame (the furniture rectangles are rebuilt per frame), so a floor beetle's height flickered between carpet and furniture top. The fix is a model change: routes are assigned at spawn and never re-derived. A beetle crawls its breach's host wall in-plane to that wall's floor crossing (floor-reaching walls are preferred as hosts; a floating host like a mirror is a last resort with one quick scripted edge-drop), then walks the floor at the height latched at its own spawn. Furniture tops are not travel surfaces any more — beetles steer around footprints on the carpet. The scanned floor height is latched too, beetle separation is applied after the surface clamp inside each beetle's own plane, and a beetle stuck for ~5 s re-plans to the floor and is counted on the Wave guard diagnostics line. The Real-plane repair diagnostics line now describes the assigned-route model, so your next paste proves it's live. Use the v10.20.1 ZIP from the download buttons at the top of this section.

New in v10.20 — Spud Frenzy, the build-up meter (the overnight train's final stage; one new mechanic, stacked on v10.19, every protected system untouched). Standard games let you build up to a short power-up window; now this one does too, in its own economy's language. Kills charge a 12-segment ring beside the pile chips — standard +1, Golden +2, HEAVY +2 — and at full charge the Keeper rolls out a crate of rejects: for 10 seconds, loads and shots are paid by the crate, not the pile. Same pinches, same HEAVY stacks, same load authority — the crate beside the pile just visibly empties while the gun glows gold and a countdown chip ticks. The meter won't recharge during its own window, the tutorial never charges it, and it composes freely with the gun augments and the orbs. The new diagnostics Frenzy line counts charges, frenzies and free shots. Use the v10.20 ZIP from the download buttons at the top of this section.

New in v10.17 — the character & world art pass (looks only, stacked on v10.16.2; no mechanics, balance or controls changed). The tuber moth is rebuilt: veined translucent wings, a fuzzy speckled body, feathery antennae, dangling legs and a wing-dust sparkle trail — no longer a generic flier. The whole roster is dressed to be named at a glance: jointed scuttling legs and glossy sheened shells throughout, armour plates on the Tank, a swollen egg abdomen on the Brood, cracked shards visible on the Husk before you ever hit it, a pulsing living throat sac on the Spitter, a taut glossy Pop, twinkling gold glints on Goldens, and a crested, warm-glowing Queen. The room got the same care: breaches tear open with jagged halo-edged cracks, crumpled dirt rims and plaster chunks at the base, their amber glow breathing slowly; scars heal as pale stitched seams; the pile's potatoes sprout; the gun's brass and varnished wood shine a little harder. The fallback ring wears the identical art. Use the v10.17 ZIP from the download buttons at the top of this section.

New in v10.16.2 — surface-conforming travel + orb/effect art (a repair + art pass, stacked on v10.16.1; placement, effects and durations unchanged). Your v10.16.1 footage showed the travel layer underneath the placement fixes misbehaving in the scanned room: beetles leaving a wall breach beelined diagonally through open air (a vertical stack descending in front of the armchair), others sank into the floor so shots splatted on the floor above them, and the Frost orb and its effect still read as white blobs. Fixed at the root: ① Conforming travel: a beetle with a host plane crawls in plane-local coordinates to that surface's floor line and is re-projected onto the surface every tick — its body is never more than ~5 cm from a legal surface — and the Carrier's trip home conforms in reverse. ② No sinking: ground beetles, floor shot-impacts, eggs, debris and mash all use the scanned floor plane's own height now, so a beetle's body and the floor your shot lands on can never disagree. ③ Orb art: Frost is a saturated ice-blue crystal (white only as glint tips); the frost effect is a jagged blue crystal shell with icicle spikes and fracture-creep texture instead of the white bubble; Frenzy shots drag golden sparkle trails; every Splash burst draws its orange radius. The fallback ring, the front-arc/inset rules, the wave guard and every protected system are untouched. Use the v10.16.2 ZIP from the download buttons at the top of this section.

New in v10.16.1 — the real-plane repair (a bug-fix pass, stacked on v10.16; nothing else changed). Your first scanned session found the one layer no earlier build had ever run: with real planes live, a breach opened on a wall behind you, its beetle crossed the room floating and upside-down over the invisible overshoot of the Quest's generous plane rectangles, your shots splatted on that invisible rim in front of it, and — as the wave's only beetle — it soft-locked the wave for ~2 minutes. All four causes are fixed at the root: ① Front-arc discipline: breaches, spawns and shot-blocking wall surfaces now test bearing against your session forward — anything behind ±90° is scenery only, on every wall, not just the one straight behind. ② Inset rectangles: each plane's collision, spawn and crawl rectangle is inset ~13% per side (furniture footprints too), so the overshoot rim is inert. ③ Crawl sanity: wall beetles orient on their surface normal — back to the room, never the upside-down flip — and clamp laterally to their host plane's real footprint. ④ Beetles before planes: a shot now resolves a beetle hit before a plane hit within a body tolerance, so a beetle near a plane's edge is always hittable. ⑤ Wave guard: ~45 s without a kill, steal, spawn or resolution while beetles live recalls the stalest one (it burrows out, the Keeper covers for it) — the wave always moves on. The fallback ring never had these defects and is byte-for-byte the same game; the frame gate, select gate, pinch hysteresis, load authority, panels, showcase and orbs are untouched. Use the v10.16.1 ZIP from the download buttons at the top of this section.

New in v10.16 — the polish pass (the last feature pass before the freeze; stacked on v10.15.5, whose five fixes, the v10.15.4 frame gate, the pinch hysteresis, the load authority and the confirm-step buttons are untouched). ① Showcase first run — the cool stuff arrives inside a judge's 5–10 minutes. Not a demo mode: the first run of a page session quietly guarantees the sightings inside normal play — exactly one tuber moth early in Round 2, exactly one Husk in Round 2, Golden Rush during Round 2, exactly one Spitter early in Round 3, and the Queen still in Round 3. Each guarantee fires at most once, only if the run reaches that point, and scripted spawns respect the beetle cap and every existing spawn rule; from the second run onward the rarity curves are the stock ones. A new diagnostics Showcase line tracks each guarantee as armed / spent / not reached. ② Orb identity — no more Jupiter. The three orb kinds that always existed (Frost / Frenzy / Splash — drop chances and effects unchanged) no longer share one white ringed ball: Frost is a pale-blue crystalline ball with icicle spikes, Frenzy a golden core with fry sticks bursting out, Splash an elongated orange sweet potato with a green sprout. Every orb wears a floating name tag naming its effect, the first drop of each kind in a session earns a one-line Keeper explanation, and collecting one stages the effect: a popup naming the effect and its size/duration, a burst at the pile, frost visibly creeping over every living beetle (an ice shell that solidifies on beetles actually frozen), and an in-world chip over the pile counting the seconds — or splash shots — down. ③ Fallback damage you can finally see. The crack network always ran (26 scars in your last paste), but on the virtual ring it read as plain portals. In fallback mode only, a growing breach now spreads crack decals across the ring surface — more and larger as its stage climbs — with an extra plaster burst and dust puff as it tears, and a patch leaves a pale seam. Real-plane mode is byte-identical; everything stays inside the existing debris / particle / scar caps, with the spread decals on their own cap of 18, swept per run. Folded in (Robert, in-headset, same evening): the room-scan instructions now give the current Horizon OS route — Settings → Environment setup → Space settings — in the in-headset Room Check notice and in the known-limits note below, replacing the older “Physical Space → Space Setup” wording (text only; the Room Check trigger and timing are unchanged). Use the v10.16 ZIP from the download buttons at the top of this section.

New in v10.15.5 — the fix pass (from your v10.15.3 headset session, your spoken report, and your screenshots — five items, nothing else touched; v10.15.4's frame gate, the pinch hysteresis, the load authority and every content module behave exactly as before). ① Panels sit in front of your chair now. Your paste proved the v10.15.2 pitch clamp worked — the results centre sat at eye level — but the panel still landed wherever your head pointed when the run ended. Panel yaw now comes from your session forward: the facing captured when the start panel is placed in the lobby. Pause, Harvest Choice, results and the tutorial card all anchor to that forward (the eye-level pitch clamp is unchanged); if a panel ever has to fall back to open-time yaw, the diagnostics Panels line says so and records the head↔panel yaw delta. ② Banners wait their turn. A story/Keeper banner no longer renders across an open panel — while any panel is up it is held (only the newest is kept; older ones are dropped, not stacked) and shown for its normal few seconds when the panel closes. ③ The last phantom path is gated. The browser's own 'select' pinch events were the one input path exempt from the v10.15.3 hysteresis; they now pass through the same gate — a select acts only if that hand has been seen open since it reappeared and is outside the ~0.35 s reacquire window. Suppressed selects are counted on the Input guard line as “select-gate”. Deliberate pinches still work via either path, de-duplicated as before. ④ The freeze has a name and a face. Your Round 4 · Wave 1 · pile 13 stop matches the hands-lost auto-pause (195 tracking dropouts that session) — except it never told you it had paused. It now shows a big “⏸ PAUSED — HANDS LOST” banner, and a new diagnostics Auto-pause line counts every auto-pause in the session with the round / wave / pile of the last one: if it happens again, the paste convicts it — or clears it and we hunt the real stall. Resume is unchanged (hands back in view). ⑤ Text fits its boxes. Your Harvest Choice photo showed the header ticker clipped mid-word and the FREE PATCH label spilling out of its green pill — both were drawn at fixed sizes outside the shrink-to-fit system. They (and the menu buttons and Ledger lines) shrink-fit now, a self-check re-measures the worst-case string for every panel element against its box, and the results panel has a fitted-scale floor: rather than shrink below it, the panel sheds the Ledger's flavour lines (never the stats) — the Panels line records the outcome.

New in v10.15.4 — a single-defect repair (from your v10.15.3 after-paste: Watchdog ×1, phase idle — “Failed to execute 'getPose' on 'XRFrame': XRFrame access outside the callback that produced it is invalid”). It never touched your play — idle phase, once, logged and bannered exactly as the watchdog policy says — but a frame-lifetime fault is a landmine: the same pattern inside a run could pause you to the menu mid-game, so the whole AR script was audited for deferred pose reads before anything was changed. The actual culprit, named: not the panels' deferred re-place (that has been loop-resident since v10.15.2 — it stores a plain timestamp and the frame loop re-places from the live camera), not the tutorial anchor, the radar or the banners (all read the renderer's camera snapshot, never a frame). The culprit was the target-ray fallback in the hand-pose block: every other pose read in the game — grip space, wrist joint, fingertip joints, detected planes — sits inside a try/catch, and that one fallback frame.getPose(targetRaySpace) call was the single unguarded read. On a healthy frame it cannot throw. On a retired frame — a teardown tick after Exit AR has set the phase to idle and the session is ending, when the earlier guarded reads have all just failed, which is precisely what routes execution down to that fallback — it threw, once, exactly as your paste recorded. The repair (three parts, no gameplay touched): ① the fallback is guarded like every sibling read — a dead frame now degrades to “no pose for that hand this tick” instead of an exception; ② pose and plane reads are skipped outright in phase idle (pre-session / teardown — idle never simulates and never needs fresh poses); ③ the loop now registers its own delivered frame as the only readable one and clears it the moment the callback returns, and the pose blocks refuse any other frame — no frame object can outlive its callback anywhere, and deferred work (panel re-place, tutorial anchor) continues to run loop-resident from the live camera, as it already did. Panels' placement behaviour, the pinch hysteresis, the load authority, comedy and content are all untouched. Verification: a Node harness ran the real AR script against a stub XRFrame that invalidates itself the moment its callback returns (any later getPose/getJointPose throws the browser's exact error): the pre-fix code reproduces your watchdog error through the idle + panel-open + re-place sequence — the retired-frame teardown tick reaches the unguarded fallback — while the fixed code runs a long mixed sequence (idle ticks including a retired frame, panel opens including the results panel and its re-place, tutorial step anchors, menu opens, restarts) with zero watchdog errors and zero invalid-frame accesses; the v10.15.2/v10.15.3 regression checks (results panel eye band through the real game-over path, ▶ PLAY arm/disarm, the Auto double-load echo refused, Skip from every tutorial step, the phantom-guard pinch sequences) all still pass in the same harness. What to watch: nothing new to test — play as you were (the content checks and the soak to 10 are still the open list). The Watchdog line in your next after-paste should read zero; if a getPose error ever appears again it will name a different phase, and that phase is the evidence. Use the v10.15.4 ZIP from the download buttons at the top of this section.

New in v10.15.3 — the fix pass (from your v10.15.1 headset session; the end-of-game menu complaint in that same report was the pre-v10.15.2 build and is already fixed there — this pass is the other two). ① The tutorial's Skip can finally be clicked. Root cause, in one line: the tutorial prompt card was re-placed from your camera every frame — 1.15 m along wherever you happened to be looking — so the card, Skip button and all, followed your aim. Turning toward Skip moved Skip; the pointer could never rest on it, exactly as you said: completely impossible. Now the card is placed once per step through the same measured-centre, eye-level anchor the panels use (the diagnostics Panels line logs it as “tutorial”), and it then stays in the world for the rest of that step — re-anchoring only when the step changes. What still moves is what should: the amber ring on the pile and the highlight on the training beetle. Skip is now an ordinary fixed gaze target, under the same 3-frame sustain rule as every panel button, and every step keeps its timeout failsafe. ② Phantom shots and loads, hardened at the detector. Your session ran Reload: Manual, yet the gun sometimes fired “without me clicking my fingers at all” and loaded unasked. The suspect mechanism lives in the joint pinch detector, which read a pinch off a single distance threshold: when a hand's joints drop out and re-enter tracking already near a pinch — or a resting hand hovers jittering across that one boundary — the detector manufactures an “edge” for a press that never happened (the same family that toggled your Sound in v10.10, which the 3-frame panel sustain only partly covered). Both pinch channels (index and middle) now run two-threshold hysteresis: a close counts only after that hand has been seen open (thumb–finger clearly apart — a press must be seen to open before it can close, so no single boundary can jitter an action), and after a hand's joints (re)appear its pinch edges are ignored for ~0.35 s while tracking stabilises — with the existing sustain rule still applying on top. Every edge the guard turns away is counted by cause on the new diagnostics Input guard line (no-open-transition / reacquire window), so your next after-paste shows the guard working — or shows zeros if the phantoms came from somewhere else, which is also evidence. The v10.15.2 load authority, panel anchoring and START confirm-step are untouched and still counting. Verification: a Node harness ran the real AR script with simulated hand joints — with the camera sweeping, the tutorial card's world position stays fixed within a step and re-anchors only on a step change; a gaze + pinch on Skip advances the tutorial from each step; a hand appearing already pinched produces no fire and no load; threshold-hover jitter produces no actions; a normal open→close pinch produces exactly one action; the HEAVY middle pinch and the two-hand menu hold still work through full simulated sequences; and the v10.15.2 checks (game-over placement, START confirm, the Auto load cycle with its echo refused) still pass. Headset confirmation is yours, as always. Test checklist: (a) Tutorial Skip from step 1: start a fresh page session (or “🎓 How to play” on the start panel), and at the very first prompt look at Skip › and pinch — the card must sit still while you aim at it, and the pinch should drop you onto the “night is yours” card. (b) A Manual game, watched: leave Reload on Manual and play — nothing may fire or load unless your fingers visibly closed from an open hand; in particular, wave a hand out of view and back in already pinched: nothing should happen. (c) The after-paste: the new Input guard line should show the suppressed-edge counts (some reacquire-window counts are normal — every hand return starts one); the Loads line should tally only loads you remember making. Use the v10.15.3 ZIP from the download buttons at the top of this section.

New in v10.15.2 — the fix pass (from your v10.13 headset session; v10.13 shares this panel and input code, so every item applies to this build). ① The results panel is centred on your eyes — really this time. Root cause, found in the geometry: the v10.12 anchor fitted the panel backdrop's height (1.86 m) and centred the panel group's origin — but in results mode the visible content is ~2.03 m tall (the backdrop sits low and the Keeper's Ledger reaches y −1.26) and its centre sits ~0.24 m below that origin. The fitted panel was under-scaled and centred low, so the Ledger's bottom landed ≈1 m below eye level — at the floor for a seated player, exactly as you described. The pause menu hides the Ledger and the start panel's content is centred on its origin, which is why only the results panel dragged. Now every panel (start / pause / Harvest Choice / results) is measured as drawn — visible content only — and its centre is placed on the clamped eye-level line (eye level to ~10° below however far you were looking, 1.5 m out, facing direction only), scaled to fit a ~40° span, and re-placed once ~0.4 s after opening in case the open-time pose was stale. Proven through the real game-over path in the harness with the camera pitched −50° at the end: before, the results panel spanned 0.20–1.39 m with its centre 0.46 m below eye level; after, it spans 0.44–1.54 m with its centre on the eye band. The diagnostics Panels line now records the anchor each panel actually used (gaze pitch → clamped centre pitch · distance · centre height · scale), so your next paste shows what the game did. ② ▶ PLAY is confirm-stepped. Your v10.13 run began from the start panel via a pinch you don't remember (lobby-integrity stayed 0 — the path was legitimate; a resting hand is the likely source, the same family as the old Exit AR issue). ▶ PLAY now gets the Exit/Restart treatment: first pinch only arms it (alarm-red, with an arm prompt, ~2.5 s), looking away or letting the window lapse disarms it, and only the second pinch starts the night. (Superseded in v10.21.29: PLAY starts on the first pinch again — see the diag-235 line.) ③ The double-load, hunted down. In Auto, “two potatoes instead of one” was real, and here is the mechanism: after an auto-load begins, a pinch arriving on the thumb+middle channel inside the load window routed straight to the HEAVY stack — a second potato on the in-flight load, and a HEAVY you never asked for. The middle-pinch gate never consulted the index channel's timestamps, and the chamber had no cross-source rule. Reproduced in the harness against the old code (one shot cycle → two potatoes → HEAVY). Now all loads pass through one authority: a stack that would ride on a load begun <0.5 s earlier from a different source is refused as a pinch echo, and the middle gate honours the index channel too. Deliberate HEAVY loads — the middle pinch (the LEFT thumb-to-middle pinch only since v10.21.28; free-hand stacking was retired with it) — work exactly as before. The diagnostics Loads line counts loads by source (manual / auto / direct HEAVY / stacks) plus every guard trip, so the next paste proves it either way. ④ This page: Enter AR, the stage, the diagnostics and the download buttons now sit at the top of this section — no more scrolling halfway down the card to start the game, read diagnostics, or grab a build; everything else follows below in its previous order. Verification: a Node harness ran the real AR script (real three.js r128, stubbed DOM/audio) — 17/17 checks: the game-over placement above; ▶ PLAY arm → start, with gaze-leave disarm; and the Auto load cycle (auto loads counted, the echo refused with the pile untouched, the deliberate stack intact). Stability systems, the comedy pass and the content modules are untouched. Use the v10.15.2 ZIP from the download buttons at the top of this section.

v10.15.1 — the Enter AR hotfix. Robert was right: v10.15 as shipped was broken, and the “complete” verdict was wrong. On the Quest the page loaded, diagnostics populated, the support check said “supported” — and tapping Enter AR did absolutely nothing, every time. Root cause, found in the code: the start panel’s new Difficulty button is drawn the moment it is created, and its label reads the difficulty config (DIFF[diffSel]) — but that config was only assigned near the end of the AR script, thousands of lines later. At draw time it didn’t exist yet, the draw threw, the whole AR script died at that line, and the Enter AR click handler — registered further down — was never attached. A dead button that looks alive. The page’s own captured console errors (“Cannot read properties of undefined (reading ‘undefined’)”, once per viewport) were this exact throw, logged and dismissed. The fix: the difficulty config now initialises before the start panel is built, the difficulty label and diagnostics reads are guarded, and a start-button label can never throw the script dead again (it falls back to the button’s name). Everything else is the v10.15 build untouched. On the file size: 670 KB was never a missing half — it is the complete game HTML; the ~1.34 MB standalone files from earlier builds carried the hub’s 688 KB decorative hero image baked in, which the AR game never loads. The game was whole; it just couldn’t start. Use the v10.15.1 ZIP from the download button below and delete the v10.15 kit. Headset confirmation still pending — the fix is verified in the code path that threw (the failing expression now resolves before first use, and the script runs to completion), but only the Quest is ground truth.

New in v10.15 — Content Pass II (the build train’s final stage; the train is complete). Three more independent named modules (v10.15 MODULE D1 / D2 / D3 in the AR code), each reachable only through typeof-guarded hooks at existing seams — strip any one by deleting its module section + its hook lines; the others, Content Pass I, the comedy pass and the base game are unaffected. All balance constants sit in one commented CONTENT15 block. ① ✨ Golden Rush — the mid-run gamble. Once per run, never in Round 1 and never during the tutorial: at a round start from Round 2 onward the Rush may begin (chance-weighted, guaranteed by Round 4) — banner, the golden shimmer sound, and the Keeper: “GOLD RUSH — they’re showing off the good potatoes!” For 20 seconds (a gold timer chip floats over the pile) the spawn scheduler favours Golden beetles, with a guaranteed count forced as the window closes, all inside the normal caps; every Golden killed during the rush pays +2 potatoes back to the pile at kill time (“+2 🥔 — the rush pays out”). It ends at 20 s or round end, whichever first. The Ledger counts Rushes / Rush gold earned. ② 🏔 Difficulty Modes — a start-panel choice. A Difficulty selector joins Sound / Aim / Reload on the start panel: COSY / STANDARD / OVERRUN, default Standard, remembered for the page session, applied from the next run start — never mid-run (the run snapshots its mode at start; the tutorial always runs at Standard). All effects flow through one DIFF config read at the existing seams: spawn interval ×1.35 / ×1.0 / ×0.75 · beetle speed ×0.9 / ×1.0 / ×1.12 · starting pile +5 / 0 / −3 (floored, never silly) · score ×0.8 / ×1.0 / ×1.5. The mode is named in the Ledger — an “Overrun night” — and grades compare within a mode. ③ 🦋 Potato Tuber Moth — the first flyer, the “look up” enemy. From Round 3, uncommon (~1 in 12 spawns, max 2 alive, counts toward the beetle cap): it enters from a breach and flutters toward the pile at head height on a wavy sine path, its altitude hard-clamped between ~15° below and ~35° above your eye line — it makes you look up, never stare at the ceiling. 1 HP; a small body with two flapping wing planes on the existing beetle rig. Reaching the pile it grabs a potato and flutters up and away, a steal like a Carrier; killed, it corkscrews down in a little spiral drop. Its first-ever appearance earns one Keeper line: “Moths. Of course there are moths.” Verification: all scripts parse; the Rush scheduler was simulated over hundreds of runs (never Round 1 or the tutorial, at most once per run, always fired by Round 4; payout +2 per rush Golden only inside the window; the chip timer ends the window at 20 s / round end); the DIFF config was exercised at every seam (spawn intervals, beetle speeds, starting piles 29 / 24 / 21, score totals for all three modes; a mid-run selector change provably does not alter the live run; the tutorial is forced to Standard); the moth was flight-simulated per-frame (spawn gating by round / frequency / alive-cap, altitude angle inside the −15°…+35° band on every sampled frame, grab-and-flee completes, cap accounting rides the shared beetles list); and the protected v10.12 set, the v10.13 comedy section and the v10.14 CONTENT14 block were diffed against the pre-pass source — byte-identical outside the new hook lines. The train, complete: v10.12 (fixes) → v10.13 (comedy) → v10.14 (Content I) → v10.15 (Content II, this build). Test this top build with the combined checklist below; v10.12–v10.14 remain available as save points — if a v10.15 item misbehaves, say which (Rush / Difficulty / Moth) and that module strips without touching the rest. (The flat 2D prototype below is unchanged in this pass — the new modules live in the AR build.)

New in v10.14 — Content Pass I (three additions from the research reserves, picked for fit-per-risk; the build train's second save point). Each item is an independent named module (v10.14 MODULE C1 / C2 / C3 in the AR code, mirrored in the 2D prototype) reachable only through typeof-guarded hooks — strip any one by deleting its module section + its hook lines; the other two, the comedy pass and the base game are unaffected. All balance constants sit in one commented CONTENT14 block (AR) / C14 block (2D). ① 🌱 Sprout-a-Spud — the economy deepens. A new Harvest Choice card, offered only when the pile holds at least 10 potatoes: picking it takes 3 potatoes off the pile immediately and plants them in a small sprouting plot beside the pile — a soil mound with a green sprout that visibly grows through the round. At round end the crop settles: no successful steal that round → it matures, +5 potatoes, a harvest popup and a Keeper line; any steal → “The crop was trampled in the raid.” and the 3 are gone. Like Patch a Breach, it competes for your one card pick — an investment, not a default. The Ledger gains running totals: Sprouts planted / harvested and Blobs intercepted. ② 🪨 Husk Beetle — crack it, then it comes for you. From Round 3, never in a round's first wave, roughly 1 in 8 spawns: a pale hard shell (a shell overlay on the existing beetle rig — no new rig) soaks 2 hits with staged cracking and no body damage; a HEAVY hit breaks it in one. The moment the shell breaks — “CRACKED!” popup, a screech through the gag limiter's family — it ENRAGES: ~2.2× speed, a straight beeline for the pile (no weaving). Under the shell it's a 1 HP body; if it reaches the pile it grabs a potato and flees at normal Carrier speed. A new decision: spend two cheap shots early, one HEAVY, or gamble on stopping a berserk beetle at the door. ③ 🟢 Spitter Beetle — the ranged threat. From Round 4, roughly 1 in 10: it advances like a normal beetle, then stops at a spit line ~2.2 m from the pile, rears, and lobs a glowing blob at the pile every ~4 s. The blob flies a visible arc (its own capped, disposed list — cap 12, counted in diagnostics). Landing on the pile splashes 1 potato away; shooting the blob mid-air destroys it for +15 and an “INTERCEPTED!” popup — the Ledger counts interceptions. The Spitter never steals directly and never closes inside its spit line; 2 HP body. Lobbing freezes with everything else while a panel is open. Verification: all scripts parse; Sprout math simulated (plant at pile 10 → −3; clean round → +5 at round end; stolen round → crop lost; card withheld below 10); Husk state machine asserted (2 cracks → break → enrage speed + beeline; HEAVY breaks instantly; body still 1 HP after the break); Spitter asserted (holds at the spit line ±tolerance, ~4 s cadence, a landed blob costs exactly 1, an interception increments its counter and destroys the blob); forced spawn spam of all three respects every hard cap; and the protected v10.12 function set (panel anchor, confirm-step, menu-gesture refund, pinch gates) plus the entire v10.13 comedy section were diffed against the pre-pass source — byte-identical.

New in v10.13 — the comedy pass (your direction: lean into the irony — the game is funnier, more unique, and more replayable for it). Six modules, each in its own named code section, each reachable only through one-line typeof-guarded hooks — any module can be stripped (delete its section + its hook lines) without affecting the others or the game, and a master COMEDY.on switch silences all of them at once. ① Keeper Narration v2: a shuffle-bag of Keeper lines keyed to events — no repeats within a run. Round-start lines escalate in desperation with the round number; the first steal of a run gets its own line; the Queen gets arrival and defeat lines; and once per run, the moment your shots fired pass your potatoes remaining, a banner lands: “Defence budget update: we have now shot more potatoes than we own.” All through the existing story-banner / popup channels — no new UI. ② The Irony Ledger: the results Ledger gains “Potatoes lost to beetles: M” beside the self-defence count, plus a verdict chosen from the comparison — “We are winning the arithmetic. Barely.” / “The beetles’ accountant sends his regards.” / “An honourable exchange rate.” ③ Comic SFX pack (synthesized through the existing audio engine, Sound toggle obeyed, amplitudes kept tasteful): a sad trombone when a Carrier escapes with a potato; a slide-whistle squeak when a HEAVY shot launches a beetle; a faint squeaky charge note as a wave spawns; an over-the-top operatic sting for the Queen's entrance — she thinks she's in a different game. One shared rate limiter: never more than one gag per ~4 seconds, never stacking. ④ Colony taunts: from Round 2, a chalk-scratched taunt appears beside the main breach for the round, escalating — NICE WALL. → SHAME ABOUT THE POTATOES. → WE CAN SEE THE PILE FROM HERE. → THE KEEPER SHOOTS LUNCH AT US. — MGMT — and beyond. One persistent mesh, raycast disabled (it can never block a shot, like the mash splats); the 2D mirror shows the same ladder as a caption by its crack. ⑤ Harvest Card quips: every Harvest Choice card — upgrades and the Queen ammo cards alike, in AR and the 2D mirror — gains a one-line Keeper subtitle (“Violence, but make it dessert.” · “Spackle: nature's apology.”). Text only; mechanics and balance unchanged; the cards grew slightly to fit, through the same panel placement as before. ⑥ Reginald: from Round 2, once per run, one ordinary beetle is Reginald — slightly larger, gold-tinted, with a small floating REGINALD name tag when he first appears. He steals and flees like any Carrier (no AI change). Shoot him and the Keeper notes “Reginald has been dissuaded.” Let him escape with a potato and next round opens with “Reginald sends his regards.” He returns every run (session memory only). Verification: all scripts parse; the shuffle-bag was simulated over 200 draws with no repeat inside a run; the taunt ladder order and the gag rate limiter were asserted under event spam; and the v10.12 anchor / refund / gesture functions were diffed against the pre-pass source — byte-identical. This is save-point one of the build train you approved: test it last, peel back here if anything's off.

New in v10.12 — the fix pass (from your v10.11 headset session; stability held, so this is four targeted fixes). ① The menu gesture no longer wastes a potato. Pinching both hands to open the menu used to fire the gun with the first pinch. Now, while both hands are pinching, no fire/load action runs at all — and because the first pinch can still land a few frames before the second hand, any shot fired by a pinch that overlapped the other hand's pinch (or began within ~250 ms before it) is refunded when the hold completes and the menu opens: the potatoes return to the pile and a still-flying shot is removed. A genuine rapid double-shot never opens a menu, so it can never be refunded. The Front door diagnostics line counts them (“menu-gesture refunds: N”). (A hand sitting pinched for seconds is treated as a resting hand, not half a gesture — it can't block your shots.) ② Panels sit at eye level now. The pause menu, Harvest Choice, results panel and start panel used to anchor to your gaze at the moment they opened — pause while looking down and the panel hung from the floor, huge and close. All four now anchor from your facing direction (yaw) only: the centre is clamped between eye level and ~12° below it no matter how far down or up you were looking, the distance is a fixed 1.5 m, and any panel taller than a ~40° vertical span at that distance is scaled down until it fits — everything readable without floor-to-ceiling head movement. Placement is still computed once, at open; panels stay put afterwards. ③ The Reload mode is visible in play. “Sometimes it auto reloaded, sometimes it didn't” traced to your settings test leaving Reload in Auto for part of the session, plus Manual's pinch-anywhere loads being invisible. The hint line floating over the pile now ends with the live mode — “Reload: MANUAL — pinch pile to load” or “Reload: AUTO — the gun loads itself” — and it redraws the moment the setting changes, from any panel. ④ The lobby question, settled by counters. You weren't sure whether a run once started by itself from the lobby. The Front door line now reports “Runs started via: ▶ PLAY ×n · ONE MORE NIGHT ×n · Restart ×n” and a lobby-integrity counter — “runs begun without START while in lobby: 0” — which increments and names the code path if any run ever begins from the lobby by any other route. It must stay 0; if it doesn't, your next diagnostics paste names the culprit. And the person you shot through: by design, not a glitch — shots only collide with scanned, stationary room geometry; people aren't in the room scan, so a shot passes through a person exactly as it passes through air. That's the behaviour you want.

New in v10.11 — the front-door pass (your two notes from Nov 12, built together). ① The lobby: tapping Enter AR used to throw you straight into a live run. Now the session opens on a start panel floating in your room — “CRITTER POTATO GUN”, the story in one sentence (The colony lives in your walls. Dawn is coming. The pile is dinner — and ammunition.), your best night from this sitting if you have one, and the three settings — Sound, Aim, Reload — adjustable right there, effective immediately, the same settings the pause menu and page buttons drive. The room, the pile and the main breach render behind it, but nothing spawns, no timer ticks, nothing steals until you gaze at 🥔 ▶ PLAY and pinch. Starting goes through the exact same run-init as Restart / ONE MORE NIGHT (the disposal sweep is now shared code), so the soak properties are unchanged; exiting and re-entering lands on the panel again, clean. A 🎓 How to play button on the panel re-runs the tutorial on demand. ② The guided first minute: on your first run of a page session the gun starts EMPTY and the Keeper teaches by doing — 1 · LOAD (the pile pulses in an amber ring; the step waits until a load actually happens) → 2 · FIRE (one single slow training beetle; the step waits for the kill) → 3 · HEAVY (middle-finger pinch; advances on a HEAVY load or after ~20 s — an advanced move never traps anyone) → 4 · MENU (two-hand pinch-hold; opening the menu once and Resuming completes it, ~20 s timeout otherwise) → DONE, and Wave 1 proceeds. Every step carries a gaze Skip › target that jumps straight to DONE, and steps 1–2 auto-advance at ~30 s — a judge can never be trapped by the tutorial. State is session-memory only; a finished/skipped tutorial changes nothing about the run. The flat 3D preview mirrors the whole flow (clicks instead of pinches, prompts as the same panel). ③ Confirm-step on Exit / Restart: from the v10.10 session analysis — a sustained resting-hand pinch sweeping the menu may have fired Exit AR. Now the first pinch on Exit AR or Restart run / ONE MORE NIGHT only arms the button: it turns alarm-red and reads “⚠ Pinch again to EXIT / RESTART”. A second pinch within ~2.5 s executes; looking away or letting the window lapse disarms it. Every other button stays single-pinch. Diagnostics gains a Front door line (current phase, tutorial step, armed state) so your next pasted panel narrates the front door too.

New in v10.10 — the emergency fix pass (the combined v10.7–v10.9 build failed its first headset test completely; this is the plain account). Bug 1 — the crash loop that looked like “the menu opens by itself.” Your diagnostics caught it exactly: Watchdog ×3, “Cannot set properties of undefined (setting ‘ephemeral’)”. Root cause, found and fixed at the source (not papered over): the game bundles three.js r128, whose Texture objects have no userData — but the v10.7 disposal system flagged per-object textures by writing tex.userData.ephemeral = true. Every score popup, story banner and Tank/Queen shell decal threw that TypeError the moment it was created — inside the frame loop, mid-run — and each watchdog recovery dropped you into the menu uninvited (your Menu-via counters prove no gesture ever misfired: two-hand ×0; the ×2 “page” openings were the recoveries). Textures now receive a userData at the single point of creation and are flagged through one helper, so the dereference cannot recur. Two more layers changed with it: idle frames no longer simulate a dead session’s leftovers (that fall-through is how the error kept re-firing in phase “idle” after Exit), and the watchdog’s recovery policy is fixed — in idle/pre-run it only logs and shows its banner, it never opens the menu; mid-run recovery stays. A same-error circuit breaker now disables the implicated system for the session after 3 identical errors (diagnostics names what was disabled) instead of recovering forever. Bug 2 — picking was still glitchy: highlight ≠ selection, panels fading. Three separate causes, three mechanical fixes: ① Selection = hover, literally. The pinch handler used to cast a fresh gaze ray at pinch time — the head has moved between the highlight frame and the pinch event, so the fresh ray could name a different button than the one the dot sat on. Pinches now activate the stored hover item itself (menuHoverId / choiceHoverIdx); no selection path re-raycasts. ② Activations with no pinch at all (your Sound toggled itself off as your head moved): the audit found no dwell timer and no hover-to-activate handler — the culprit was the joint-pinch detector firing on a single frame of tracking noise as a resting lap hand crossed the edge of the tracking volume, which head pitch does constantly. While any panel is open, a joint-detected pinch must now be sustained for 3 frames to count; the browser’s own select event stays immediate, and hover alone can never activate anything. ③ The fade in/out: every panel material was transparent, depth-write off, with no render order, so the renderer re-sorted the stack by head angle each frame and the backdrop periodically drew over the buttons. Panels are now opaque backdrops with depth writes and a pinned render order — identical from every head pose. Floating text (from your v10.6 memory, confirmed in code): the worst offender was the pile hint line — a 1.6 m-wide sprite whose text was ~40% wider than its canvas and clipped at both ends — with long score popups (“THE QUEEN RELEASES A RING OF LARVAE!”) clipping the same way. All in-AR text sprites now shrink-to-fit their measured string, and sprite scales are capped (hint 1.15 m, popups 0.52 m, story banner 1.5 m), outline treatment unchanged. Room Check (new, display-only): ~10 s into a session with still zero detected planes, a one-time in-headset notice says the game is on its virtual ring and points at Space Setup (any pinch dismisses it); if hands-lost pauses you twice in one run, that panel adds a brighter-light line. Regression: this pass ships with a headless harness that steps the real frame loop through idle-with-live-session state (600 frames), menu-open and at-cap playing states, sweeps the gaze across every panel toggle with zero pinches (asserting nothing changes), and pinches a highlighted toggle (asserting exactly one activation of exactly that item) — all clean before this page was rebuilt.

New in v10.7 — the fix pass (from your v10.6 headset test): ① The freeze: the leading suspect was real — restarts removed objects from the scene but never disposed their GPU geometry/materials, and every score popup minted a fresh canvas texture that lived forever. After several runs the frame loop choked. Now every per-run list is disposed on restart and hard-capped with oldest-first eviction (particles 140, debris 40, splats 8, eggs 24, popups 14, beetles 42). A frame-loop watchdog catches any future frame error, logs it (message + phase + live object counts) to diagnostics, shows a “Recovered from a hiccup” banner in-headset and recovers to the menu — a freeze can never be silent again. Diagnostics gains a live object-counts line, refreshed every second. And if both hands lose tracking for 3+ seconds, the game auto-pauses behind a big HANDS LOST panel and resumes when your hands return — no more dead world. ② Menu refined: the floating MENU button is deleted (your call) — in-AR opening is the two-hand pinch-hold (1 s) only. And the single-cursor rule: while any menu/choice/results panel is open, the gun holsters out of sight and its aim ray hides; the gaze dot is the only pointer, and hover highlight and pinch selection read that same ray — the highlighted item is the pinch target. Hitboxes are now larger than the drawn buttons. ③ Radar donut fixed: the band torus was tilted through the face. The tracker is rebuilt as a watch — the face sits proud on a case on top of your wrist, the band wraps behind it (band surface reaches z +0.014 at most, behind the case front at +0.016 and the face at +0.0165) and can never cover the screen. ④ Chair beetles: wall/furniture-crawling beetles sat half-sunk in their surface with their hit centre inside it; they now render proud of the surface (logical position = mesh position) and a shot’s surface allowance is the beetle’s own body radius — see the known-limits note in the audit for the un-scanned-chair case.

New in v10.8 — the full audit & hardening pass (no new features): every phase transition, XR session start/end/re-entry, listener, timer, allocation and input path was audited end to end (AR + 2D mirror). Fixed: session-end now tears down mid-Choice/mid-Queen/hands-lost state; Enter AR can't double-start; a hidden page auto-pauses a live run; joint pinch state resets on select-end; poisoned (NaN) positions are removed instead of propagated; the aim ray no longer allocates a GPU buffer every frame; the 2D mirror got the same caps. Verified clean and documented — with the feature inventory (present / partial / absent, research reserves included) and honest known-limits — in the Audit v10.8 section below.

New in v10.9 — charm & retention (researched, additive only): built from the second research pass (sources listed in the Audit section addendum). ① The Keeper’s Ledger on the results panel: score, round, beetles squashed, accuracy, best combo/chain, clutch saves, potatoes left — and the signature line, “Potatoes shot in self-defence” (your shots fired: in this game your ammo is the harvest). ② A grade for the night (S/A/B/C/D) computed honestly from score + potatoes left + accuracy + rounds, with the gap in potatoes: “4 potatoes short of an A.” ③ A near-miss line on every loss — the Queen’s remaining HP, the grade gap, or your best-round distance; a loss always pays out the Ledger + grade + line before the retry. ④ One reactive line per run: the Keeper comments on how the last run ended (a carrier that got away has a name now: Gerald), and the Queen remembers — beaten her in an earlier run this sitting and her entry banner says so. ⑤ Next-unlock proximity: one line naming the nearest unearned thing (Sweet rounds, Fry mode, the next grade, your best score). Persistence judgement, stated plainly: bests live in session memory only — no localStorage — so nothing can fail stale or blocked in a headset context; they cover a sitting’s “one more night” loop and reset with the page. ⑥ Beetle micro-personality: a carrier does a two-hop celebration when it grabs a potato and glances back once mid-flee; during Harvest Choice, breach eyes peek — and duck when your gaze lands on them. Root transforms only; locomotion untouched. ⑦ Pile & wall life: the pile jiggles as a beetle closes in and trembles under 7 potatoes; a wall miss near a breach kicks up dust and startles eyes open in it; breach scars now persist for the whole session, so your walls keep the night’s story across runs. ⑧ One More Night: the results panel’s primary button is now a big ONE MORE NIGHT — same settings, straight back in — and the wrist radar carries a “BEST NIGHT: ROUND n PACE” marker (a stat line, never a recorded ghost). Explicitly deferred (research’s stability warnings): daily seeded runs, Spicy-Night modifiers, Ascension/Endless modes, the Field Guide album, ghost recording, Queen AI changes, new-mesh cosmetics.

New in v8 — the gameplay-depth pass (from your last test): ① Furniture counts now: a detected tabletop/desk plane (a horizontal plane well above the floor) is a climbable surface — beetles climb its edge, cross the top, and climb down — or an obstacle floor paths steer around, instead of crawling through the object. ② Reload anywhere: pinch with your loading hand anywhere to load — no more looking down at the pile (the loading hand is the LEFT hand since v10.21.28); the potato still arcs visibly from the pile into the gun and still costs from the pile. ③ Aim: Hand / Head toggle in the pause menu and below — Head aims the gun along your gaze (the feel you said was easier), Hand aims from your arm. ④ HEAVY double-load: thumb-to-middle-finger pinch loads two potatoes (cost 2) — one huge splat shot that one-shots a Tank, with splash. A quick double-pinch with the gun hand does the same if the middle pinch doesn't read. ⑤ Power-ups: Golden and Carrier kills sometimes drop a glowing orb — shoot it for French Fry Frenzy (8 s rapid fire, no reload) or Sweet Splash (next 5 shots splash).

New in v10 — the fun pass (from the mechanics research you asked for): ① Juice everywhere: kills squash flat under a white flash with shell chunks flying; splat sounds climb a pitch ladder as your combo grows (and a “combo banked” chime lands when a big chain ends); HEAVY kills freeze the beetles for a heartbeat; Tanks stagger on every hit and their shells crack in stages — no more silent sponges. Callouts float for long shots, chains and heavy kills. The shake lives on the gun and the pile only — your room stays rock-steady. ② Mash splats: a shot that misses and hits the floor, a tabletop — or, since v10.1, a wall — leaves a pulp splat for ~6 s: beetles crossing it crawl at half speed, wall-crawlers included, because the shot's flight is now tested against the real wall planes and the splat sticks flush to the wall it hit, with a slight downward smear. A miss still costs a potato, but it buys a little ground now — on whatever surface it lands. ③ Harvest Choice: clear a round and the action freezes on 3 big cards — pinch one: Stockpile, Bigger Splash, Light Heavy, Lucky Charm, Longer Frenzy, Sticky Mash, Steady Hands or Golden Touch.
